notes: The author describes the action of tau on the three generators and calls it an automorphism of the loop group of signature -1, satisfying tau^2=1. He states that it commutes with the permutation-group action “mod autom extérieurs”, and that this gives the canonical outer action of the product with {±1}, denoted Gamma_0,3. These assertions and the terminology extérieurs are transcribed without correction or verification.

He then considers exterior automorphisms commuting with rho. An interlinear qualification says that the relevant exterior automorphism normalizes the conjugacy class of the object preferentially read l_0, with the blind audit retaining tout as a local graphic alternative. He chooses a representative u normalizing L_0, describes L_0 as isomorphic to the profinite integers generated by l_0, and states that u is unique “mod composition par un lambda in L_0”. The word composition is clear and is not changed to H’s conjugaison.

The author introduces the multiplier p, with an added p=chi(u), writes u(l_0)=l_0^p, and introduces g through u rho=int(g) rho u after cancelling an earlier rho u immediately after the equals sign. The last line begins an explanation of the uniqueness of g and ends at u étant. No continuation is supplied.

There is no date and no explicit authorial doubt phrase on this sheet. The top page number is 2 and the bottom-left number is 6. No authorial mathematical slip was established by this reading. No targeted proof, independent re-proof or computation was performed.

The two supplied C marks M0780 and M0781 remain unresolved alphabet distinctions. The cancelled un remains doubtful. The blind audit further marks whether the est cluster is a whole-word replacement or a partial cancellation. The separate mathematical deletion rho u is retained as a doubtful recovery after the blind audit: its rho stem is visible, but the crossed u is not wholly separable.

The class-normalizing phrase is physically between the Notons que line and the tout autom extérieur provient line, in smaller darker writing, with no visible guide. Its attachment after extérieur follows the most immediate local placement but should be reviewed as an insertion-location decision. The equality chi(u) has a guide that starts after p. Its small comma-like upper-line mark and the guide endpoint are close; the proposed comma stays with the added text rather than the main membership expression.

H’s uncertainties for groupe and n’est autre do not require substantive change rows because the textual readings agree; those words were read on the image. H’s trailing illegibility placeholder corresponds to no further ink. The final line and lower margin are preserved in a shared adjudication crop.

The whole image and the two supplied halves were each inspected once. Twelve distinct first-reading crops were made for witness disagreements, open readings and the mathematical cancellation. No OCR, external research, other scan packet or other reader report was consulted. No TeX compilation was run.

Main-reader adjudication accepts the comma as part of the upper-line addition: it is above the hatted-Z expression and separate from the long curved guide. The cancellation in the final display retains rho u as its preferred recovery, now with explicit doubt on the partly obscured product. The doubtful prose cancellations un and est remain doubtful. No mathematical verification is claimed on this page.

Blind second-reading adjudication resolves the indexed initial group as capital Pi from its cap and two legs together with the already established indexed definition. The unindexed pi in Soit g has a curved right foot and is retained. Several independent prose alternatives were rejected from visible tall letters and low joins, while the final object of the interlinear normalizing clause, the scope of the est correction and the cancelled rho-u remain uncertain. No proof or computation was performed in this audit.
